messages.author: 5a0b58acc30db175
messages.subject: Re: using categorical data in occu
parts:
Hi Clinton,

I can't specifically comment on your categorical covariate question (it looks like a coding issue - have you classified it as a 'factor'?) but the 'Hessian and starting value' error I'm familiar with and has been covered in some detail in these two threads:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/unmarked/occupancy$20data/unmarked/C4s5TVAnW8o/Bi09OWam2K0J

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/unmarked/hessian$20/unmarked/uBvWCtDy8aE/OUnfdTfscUwJ

Maybe those threads can generate some solutions.

Cheers, Erik

On Friday, February 15, 2013 1:20:06 PM UTC-6, Clinton wrote:
Hello all-

I would like to include strata definitions (stand codes of forest types) within a model and have a few general questions:

1) It is okay to use alpha categorical data in a model correct?

2) If so, how can you avoid scaling that particular covariate and keep it in the .UMF
   For example, I tried

siteCovs(bith12.umf)<-scale(siteCovs(bith12.umf)[,-3])

and this scaled all of my covariates but entirely removed my column of interest (3=strata)

3) I manually scaled a subset of covariates and ran a model containing strata data and received the following error:

> (fm3 <- occu(~date+time ~elev+strata, bith12.umf))
Error: Hessian is singular.  Try providing starting values or using fewer covariates.

Is this due to "strata" being a alpha categorical variable, or ????

Thanks.

messages.author: 8a9077d20d056615
messages.subject: Re: using categorical data in occu
parts:
Thanks for the tip Erik.

You were correct, the issue was in my coding. I needed to remove the intercept from the "strata" category by "-1"

> (fm3 <- occu(~date+time ~elev+strata-1, bith12.umf))

No need to address the "Hessian and starting value error"

-Clint

messages.subject: Re: using categorical data in occu
parts:
Back to the original question (2): I'm still unsure how to code for omitting a variable when group scaling a .UMF

For example: I have the following observational covariates in a unmarked frame.

(obscovs=list
        (obs=blpw10.data[,c("obsY1V1","obsY1V2", "obsY1V3")],
        time=blpw10.data[,c("timeY1V1","timeY1V2","timeY1V3")],
        date=blpw10.data[,c("dateY1V1","dateY1V2", "dateY1V3")],
        sky=blpw10.data[,c("skyY1V1","skyY1V2", "skyY1V3")],
        wind=blpw10.data[,c("windY1V1","windY1V2", "windY1V3")],
        temp=blpw10.data[,c("tempY1V1","tempY1V2", "tempY1V3")])
        ))

When I try to scale using:

obsCovs(blpw10.umf)<- scale(obsCovs(blpw10.umf))

I get the error:

Error in colMeans(x, na.rm = TRUE) : 'x' must be numeric

because 'obs' is a factor and non numeric. I have named 'obs' as.factor and it seems to go into the .UMF fine. How can I scale all of the covariates except 'obs'?

Thanks.
